title: Teenage 'detectives' hijacking liquor and hiring the band for hot shots
summary: Teenage gangs near Shreveport confiscate liquor from train passengers and hire Love's group to play at woods parties for pay.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You know, they had a set of teenage boys there. They got a little junction before you get to Shreveport on the teepee, you know. The train goes halfway around, turn around and back into Shreveport, you see. And them fellas coming from Monroe, they got kind of strict on that liquor business that searched. They had caught a fella with a bass violin full of liquor, you see. And that run along, run along, when them teenage boys had a gang. They'd get together and they'd go out to the junction and play detective, you know. There was no detective. They'd go out there and confiscate a lot of liquor from them people, you know. That your grip up there? The fella said, yeah. Get it down, open it up. The fella opened it up, give me the grip. Confiscate that liquor, bring it to the city hall. That your grip up there? The fella said, no, I ain't got no grip. You get it down and look in it anyhow. It would be hit for the fellas sometime, you know. You'd look in there and you'd find the liquor and the fella disowned it. Well, he couldn't rest it. He just confiscated liquor, just take it. Put it in an automobile. We was waking at the Starfield, you know, them teenage boys. Here they come. Y'all want to make a little hot shot tonight? That's what they call it. Just go out with them and play a little music on the side road out the city. I said, yeah, how much in it? I said, what y'all charge? About three hours. No one of those big bands, this one was a cornet and a fiddle, a guitar, something like that. I said, about $15 a man. I said, all right. We'll come by and pick you up in the fold. What time do they get off? We'd be on duty. We'd be off at 10.30. They'd come around and pick us up. Go around through town, pick some other fella up and out they go. They know where they're going, you see. The other fella, the other girl, they go around and steal them girls out the house. And bring them out in the woods then, man. And get out there, man. They'd have a tour of the bands. They'd run off the highway way down on the side road. They had a regular picnic out there and some of them would go by the drugstore and bring the ginger ale and mix alcohol and whiskey and everything. Oh man, they'd have the time and they'd get to fighting, you know. They'd fight and everything. And they'd say, how much you charge to play another hour? I'd say about three dollars. We'd play another hour for you for three dollars. Beansbury out there already, you know. We'd keep that job, you know. We'd make plenty of money on them fellas. And now them fellas pay that, you know. The fellas say, you better pay us off. Now I say, because you all might get drunk and we don't get our money. Yeah, we'll get it up. They'll get the money up. We'll pay another hour, you know. Then after they get enough, get tired and everything, while we come home. About once or twice a week we'd have them jobs. But we didn't know what them fellas was doing. We found that out after. They broke it up. They caught a lot of them. We thought they was buying that liquor or something like that. It was playing detective. Hijacking that. Yeah. That musician sees some funny things.
